Childhood Memory

Recollections  · 23 Oct 2025

When I was a child, there was a stretch of meadow near my home. Through the turning of seasons, it blossomed with wild clover, dandelions, foxtails, snakeberries, asters, and ground ivy, an intimate, untamed world breathing beneath the clouds.

In spring, I remember a pond hidden behind the hill. A winding wooden bridge led to a little pavilion at its heart, where passersby sometimes paused to rest. I found tadpoles there, kept them in large glass jars, and watched as they grew their tiny legs, the silent miracle of transformation unfolding in my hands.

By the pond stood a great tree with a wasp’s nest in its branches. On still summer nights, the chorus of cicadas rose and fell, the loudest voice of the landscape. The basketball court nearby was always empty; I never saw anyone play there. I would cling to the hoop, my feet balanced on the bolts and screws that held it to the ground. Not far away stood two rows of tall plane trees, solemn and proud.

When autumn rain fell, their leaves blanketed the path in golden brown, and footsteps carved a road through them. The air was thick with the scent of earth and its muddy fragile underbelly, a smell that deepened in late harvest and slowly faded as winter drew near.

Winter was the season of imaginations. At the end of the sycamore path stood a half-open wooden door, not the main entrance; I never saw that one. The adults said it was on the other side of the wall, outside the school grounds. But within those walls, was the entirety of my childhood.

With a small shovel, I scraped away winter bit by bit, sending snow tumbling from my balcony onto the one below, where a new birth was waiting to form.

Then spring would quietly return, softly brushing the earth awake. And I would find myself a step closer to adolescence, to adulthood, a step closer to leaving home. The seasons of last year had barely been savored before my shoes grew tight, my hair grew longer, my shadow stretched further, and my skin grew layers, as did my thoughts.

When night fell, I ran beneath dim starlight, chasing my lengthened shadow. Behind every closed curtain, I envisioned silhouettes of the protagonists, the undercover antagonists, some running, some gazing, some simply existing, hustling, full, alive and whole.

By Yu Shi, 02/05/2023, in Des Moines, IA
